system_description.narrative_title: A Fracturing, Interdependent World: War, Markets and Tech at Risk
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system under strain from overlapping kinetic conflicts, strategic sabotage and proxy warfare, rising great‑power competition over technology and critical supplies, and volatile political shifts that reconfigure alliances. Energy and shipping disruptions, attacks on commercial and space infrastructure, and financial-market stress amplify feedbacks that make local crises spill rapidly across regions and markets.
system_description.scope: State and non‑state actors, regional conflict theatres (Ukraine, Middle East, Sahel, Korea), major‑power rivalry (US, China, Russia), global markets and finance, critical technologies and infrastructure (satcom, rare earths, shipping lanes, energy systems), international institutions and mediation channels.
system_description.super_system: The planetary political‑economic‑security system of globalisation and interdependent supply chains and markets.
adjacent_subsystems: Regional conflict theatres (Middle East, Ukraine/Russia, Korea, Africa)
Global economic and financial system (bond markets, currencies, trade flows)
Global technology and critical‑infrastructure network (satellites, semiconductors, rare earths)
Energy and commodity supply networks (oil, LNG, shipping routes, storage)

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with NATO and other Western backers, are locked in a protracted high‑intensity war featuring cross‑border strikes, energy and shipping disruptions, and episodic ceasefires that are shifting military dynamics and external involvement.

variables.name: Iran-led regional escalation
variables.description: Iran and its proxy networks (including Houthi and Hezbollah elements), Israel, Gulf states and the United States are engaged in an expanding campaign of proxy strikes, maritime and aerial attacks, and diplomatic manoeuvres that is raising the risk of wider Middle East conflagration.

variables.name: U.S.-China strategic rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting economic and technological primacy through trade and investment controls, supply‑chain leverage (rare earths, semiconductors), grey‑zone pressure around Taiwan and diplomatic influence campaigns, reshaping global alliances and markets.

variables.name: Global energy market volatility
variables.description: World oil and refined‑products markets, producers and buyers are undergoing recurring supply shocks, shipping‑route and storage disruptions, and policy responses (reserves, stockpiling, refinery re‑routing) that are reconfiguring energy-security calculations and price dynamics.

variables.name: Electoral and political realignments
variables.description: A wave of electoral shocks, populist comebacks and protest-driven changes in democracies (exemplified by contests in Brazil, Serbia and Israel) is producing sudden policy shifts, contested mandates and altered external partnerships that increase geopolitical uncertainty.
